annotations.text:
Two problems, not one.

The medium was wrong -- stroked vector in a game of PixelGrids. But flat pixel shapes read as diagrams too. The fix is a lit object in a bezel: something to be lit against, and six value steps instead of three.

The frame is code, the object is art.

Bezel, ground, cast shadow and sheen are generated from the talent's category. Thirty-seven talents cost thirty-seven objects -- roughly a day -- not thirty-seven illustrations.

Four of the seven failed as drawings first.

SPLIT SHAFT was an axe, then a goblet, then a spanner -- every time because the head was as broad as it was long. LONG THROW was a fire extinguisher until it became a bundle. What fixes these is proportion, not detail.

The abstract talents are still open.

QUICK TONGUE is a shorter cooldown and BIG COMBO is a bigger radius: no object exists for either. The colour code carries some of it now -- a green square already says attack speed -- but the square still needs something in it.
